title: Lines and Angles: Points, Rays, Segments and Angles
seo_title: Lines and Angles Class 6 Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 2)
standard_text: Points, lines, line segments and rays; angles as turns; measuring angles; types of angles (acute, right, obtuse, straight and reflex) (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 6)
meta_desc: Class 6 Lines and Angles worksheet (Ganita Prakash Chapter 2): points, lines, rays and segments, types of angles, turns, clocks and angles on a line. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A right angle is 90°; a straight angle is 180°
body_html:
How it works

A line segment has two endpoints, a ray has one endpoint and goes on in one direction, and a line goes on in both directions.

An angle is made by two rays from a common point (the vertex). It measures the amount of turn: a full turn is 360°, a half turn 180°, a quarter turn 90°.

Types: acute (less than 90°), right (90°), obtuse (between 90° and 180°), straight (180°), reflex (more than 180°).

Example

What type of angle is 135°?

Between 90° and 180°

Answer: Obtuse

Example

Angles on a straight line are x and 65°. Find x.

180° − 65°

Answer: 115°

Common mistakes

  • Calling a ray a line segment (a ray has only one endpoint).
  • Calling 90° obtuse or acute. It is a right angle.
  • Reading the wrong scale of the protractor (40° instead of 140°).

faq.q: What is the difference between a line, a ray and a segment?
faq.a: A segment has two endpoints, a ray has one, and a line has none — it goes on in both directions.

faq.q: What are the types of angles?
faq.a: Acute (less than 90°), right (90°), obtuse (90° to 180°), straight (180°) and reflex (180° to 360°).

items.q: Which is another name for line GD?
items.e: Any two points on a line name it. F and D are both on the line, so line FD is the same line.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: It has two endpoints and no arrows. It is segment MP, written MP.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: It has two endpoints and no arrows. It is segment KH, written KH.

items.q: 3 points are marked on a line. How many segments have two of these points as endpoints?
items.e: Each pair of points is the endpoints of one segment: 3 × 2 ÷ 2 = 3. Short segments and long ones both count.

items.q: 4 points are marked on a line. How many different rays start at one of these points and go through another one of them?
items.e: Rays that start at the same point and go the same way are the same ray. So each point gives one ray to the right (except the last) and one to the left (except the first): 2 × 3 = 6.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: It has two endpoints and no arrows. It is segment QR, written QR.

items.q: The ray starts at S and goes through R and Q. Which is another name for it?
items.e: A ray is named by its endpoint first, then any other point on it. The endpoint is S, so ray SR is the same ray.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: It has one endpoint, H, and goes on forever through G. A ray is named endpoint first: ray HG.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: It has one endpoint, Z, and goes on forever through Y. A ray is named endpoint first: ray ZY.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: It has one endpoint, T, and goes on forever through U. A ray is named endpoint first: ray TU.

items.q: Two different planes intersect. What is their intersection?
items.e: Two planes that cross meet in a line, like two walls meeting at a corner.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: Arrows on both ends: it goes on forever both ways. It is line MK.

items.q: 4 points are marked on a line. How many segments have two of these points as endpoints?
items.e: Each pair of points is the endpoints of one segment: 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 6. Short segments and long ones both count.

items.q: Two different lines intersect. What is their intersection?
items.e: Two different lines can cross at only one place, so they meet in a point.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: It has one endpoint, W, and goes on forever through U. A ray is named endpoint first: ray WU.

items.q: 8 points are marked on a line. How many different rays start at one of these points and go through another one of them?
items.e: Rays that start at the same point and go the same way are the same ray. So each point gives one ray to the right (except the last) and one to the left (except the first): 2 × 7 = 14.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: It has one endpoint, J, and goes on forever through L. A ray is named endpoint first: ray JL.

items.q: There are 7 points in a plane, and no three of them are collinear. How many lines can you draw through pairs of these points?
items.e: Each pair of points makes one line. The number of pairs is 7 × 6 ÷ 2 = 21. Do not count line AB and line BA twice.

items.q: 10 points are marked on a line. How many different rays start at one of these points and go through another one of them?
items.e: Rays that start at the same point and go the same way are the same ray. So each point gives one ray to the right (except the last) and one to the left (except the first): 2 × 9 = 18.

items.q: What is the name of this figure?
items.e: It has one endpoint, D, and goes on forever through G. A ray is named endpoint first: ray DG.

items.q: How many degrees is one-third of a turn?
items.e: A full turn is 360°, so one-third of a turn is 120°.

items.q: You face East and turn 180° anticlockwise. Which way do you face now?
items.e: Each 90° is a quarter turn. You face West.

items.q: You face East and turn 270° clockwise. Which way do you face now?
items.e: Each 90° is a quarter turn. You face North.

items.q: What is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock at 11 o'clock?
items.e: Each hour mark is 30°. 1 hour apart → 30°.
